solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Divine manifestation in Bible seen by a sailor

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A vision of a god appears in Scripture to a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief a deity descending to earth in bodily form is given this name.

clue.text: Scotsman conveys message from Cockney murderers wanting death penalty

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the initial aitch, so the H goes

parts.note: killers seeking execution would say hang us

explanation.surface: A Scot relays a London gangsters' plea to be executed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop their aitches, so the plea 'hang us' becomes 'ang us.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Scottish male first name, so it can stand for a Scotsman.

clue.text: Like a sort of fat princess turning up to model

parts.note: Di was the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales
to pose is to model for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A rather plump princess arrives for a modelling session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' means arriving, not a reversal; 'sort of fat' is an adjectival phrase, fatty.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes fatty tissue in the body, so it means somewhat fat or fatty.

clue.text: I hit on ancestry unexpectedly — something obtained from old documents?

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so the letters fall into a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A genealogist stumbles on family roots while poring over old papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Study of the distant past relies on old records; the question mark flags a loose, example-style definition.

clue.text: Bird with curvaceous shape, pale

parts.note: the letter S has a curving, sinuous form
wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: A white bird with a graceful curving neck is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A large long-necked waterbird, a straightforward example of a bird.

clue.text: Complete failure brings a yell after win initially

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind that first letter
initially means the first letter of win is taken

parts.note: a shout is a yell

explanation.surface: A victory celebration ends in a total flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop or fiasco; the word derives from a match abandoned because of rain.

clue.text: Fantastic caress when beset by desire mounting? It's essential

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the desire goes around the shuffled caress
mounting means rising, so in a down clue the word for desire is read upwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful, so the letters of caress are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wonderful caress amid rising desire is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounting' reads the desire word upwards; 'when' is only a link and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something required and indispensable, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fox in marshy territory with endless audacity

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land

indicators.note: endless means losing its last letter, so the word for audacity is cut short

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek or audacity

explanation.surface: A fox roams the marshland with boundless cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A small desert fox of North Africa with very large ears, an example of a fox.

clue.text: Sorcerer and hag hop around — we map out the steps

indicators.note: around means moving about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A wizard and a witch dance about, while someone plans the routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance designers plan out the steps and movements that performers follow, so the definition describes their work.

clue.text: At extremities girl experiences irritation produced by bugs

indicators.note: at its extremities means only the first and last letters of the word girl are taken

parts.note: someone who itches feels skin irritation

explanation.surface: A girl's skin irritation is caused by insect bites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bugs' reads as insects but is the definition: faults in software or machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs in computing are faults or malfunctions, a common synonym for minor technical errors.

clue.text: Sophy sick? Out-of-date medicine has contributed to that

indicators.note: the words Sophy sick each give part of the letters, so together they contribute the word sought

explanation.surface: Is Sophy ill? Some old-fashioned remedy may be to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic word for a medicinal drug, especially a purgative, hence out-of-date.

clue.text: Agent restricted by bungling managers

indicators.note: restricted by means held within, so the letters lie inside the words bungling managers

explanation.surface: A spy is held back by incompetent bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A US slang term for an FBI agent, short for government man.

clue.text: Jiggery-pokery may be hatched up in men's dark room, sir

indicators.note: a scheme hatched up is contrived, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Some trickery is plotted in a darkened men's room, addressed to a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean deceptive trickery and distraction meant to fool onlookers.

clue.text: Port makes bishop relax

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: A harbour town lets a churchman take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval port in Brittany, north-western France, an example of a harbour city.

clue.text: Support not weighing much that may be used by photographer

definitions.text: that may be used by photographer

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
something light has little weight

explanation.surface: A lightweight stand is the sort a photographer might use.
explanation.definitionFit: Illumination from behind the subject is a lighting technique used in photography.

clue.text: Groups of bodies of soldiers in various actions

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed in among the reshuffled letters of actions
various suggests differing arrangements, so the letters of actions are reordered

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Bands of troops take part in assorted military operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldiers' gives OR, other ranks, the usual crossword abbreviation for non-officers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are associations of several companies or organisations working together, hence groups of bodies.

clue.text: Tea is served, securing link with voluntary organisations

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: securing means holding in, so the word is wraps around the link

parts.note: taken as written
a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: Tea is handed round, cementing a connection with volunteer groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' is surface padding linking the pieces; CHAR is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodies run for good causes rather than profit, often staffed by volunteers.

clue.text: Plant needs a way to absorb potassium over time

indicators.note: over means above, so in a down clue these letters sit on top of the time
to absorb means to take in, so the way takes in potassium

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A plant needs a route by which to take up potassium over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant of the borage family whose root yields a red dye, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Thought from political assistant first to be dropped

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped down, so in this down clue it falls to the bottom

parts.note: an aide is an assistant to a politician

explanation.surface: An idea comes from a political aide about to be sacked first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' reads as fired, but means moved lower: the first letter goes to the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or concept in the mind, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A bit of cake maybe cut for a ruler

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter of the fruit word is lost

parts.note: a sultana is a dried grape found in fruit cake

explanation.surface: A slice of cake perhaps is cut for a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim sovereign, so a ruler by example.

clue.text: Bank keeping quiet when response is demanded

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the bank surrounds the quiet sign

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A bank stays silent although an answer is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun, a lender or riverside, but is the verb, to count on.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer given to a question or letter, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rep unexpectedly tight-lipped about one bonus payment

indicators.note: unexpectedly means surprisingly, so the letters of rep fall into another order
about means around, so the silent word goes round one

parts.note: mum means silent, saying nothing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sales rep, surprisingly quiet, receives a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight-lipped' means keeping quiet, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum added to the usual amount, as a reward or extra charge, a synonym of bonus.

clue.text: Quickly appreciate positive audience reaction

parts.note: to like something is to appreciate it
an audience that reacts well applauds, giving those clapping

explanation.surface: A performer enjoys an audience's warm applause.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the phrase means enjoy those who applaud. 'Like the clappers' is British slang for very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal idiom meaning very fast, as in running at great speed.

clue.text: Elder denied one European title

indicators.note: denied means refused, so the elder loses the numeral

parts.note: a senior is an older person, an elder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An older man is refused a particular European honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish form of address equivalent to Mr, a title used in Europe.

clue.text: Dope with endeavour to join the aristocracy

parts.note: dope and gen are both slang for information
to try is to endeavour

explanation.surface: Someone takes drugs while trying to climb into high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs, but here means inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper class, people of good birth just below the nobility, is an established sense.

clue.text: Peculiar larvae in plant

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly into another order

explanation.surface: Odd grubs are found inside a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering herb whose root is used as a sedative, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Shoddy stuff at back of the gallery?

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods

indicators.note: at the back of a word is its last letter, here of the

explanation.surface: Is there cheap rubbish stored behind the art gallery?
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is a well-known British art museum, named after the sugar magnate Henry Tate.

clue.text: Chemical compound is getting Rome fouled up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fouled up means messed up, so the letters of Rome are jumbled

explanation.surface: A chemical substance is causing pollution in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule with the same atoms as another but arranged differently, a type of compound.
